title: A Big Test for Britain's Leader: Local Elections Could Shake Things Up!
summary: Have you ever had a day where everything felt like a big test? That's what Thursday was like for Keir Starmer, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. Voters all across England, Scotland, and Wales went to polling stations to choose about 5,000 local councilors and some mayors. It's the biggest election since Labour won in a huge landslide in July 2024. But now, many people are unhappy. Starmer's popularity has dropped a lot. His government hasn't been able to fix the economy or make life cheaper, and things got even harder when a war between the US, Israel, and Iran messed up oil shipments. Plus, he made a really unpopular choice: he picked Peter Mandelson—a friend of a man named Jeffrey Epstein, who was involved in a terrible scandal—to be the UK's ambassador to the US. Now, Labour is worried they might lose many of the 2,500 council seats they're defending. Some Labour members even tried to push Starmer out in February. If the results are bad, rivals like Health Secretary Wes Streeting could challenge him. But the story isn't just about Labour. A newer party called Reform UK, led by Nigel Farage, is expected to win a lot of votes from working-class areas. The Green Party might also gain hundreds of seats. One expert said this could be the end of the old two-party system where only Labour and the Conservatives mattered. Farage even said a strong result for Reform could mean Starmer is "gone by the middle of summer." Votes were being counted overnight, with most results coming Friday. It's a nervous wait—like waiting for your own report card!
why_it_matters: The people elected to local councils make choices about your parks, schools, and community centres, so these elections help shape the places where kids live and play.

background_read: Keir Starmer became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in July 2024 after his Labour Party won a huge election victory. Before that, the Conservative Party had led for 14 years.
Local councils in Britain are like student councils for towns; they make decisions about parks, libraries, schools, and rubbish collection. The people who run them are called councilors.

Nigel Farage is a British politician known for leading the campaign to leave the European Union, often called Brexit. His Reform UK party mainly appeals to voters who feel unhappy with the bigger parties.
